title: Bootstrapped Robustness Assessment for Qualitative Comparative Analysis
text: braQCA R package provides bootstrapped robustness tools Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA). QCA set-theoretic, case-oriented method widely used political science, sociology, comparative policy research identify combinations conditions sufficient necessary outcome. persistent challenge QCA truth table algorithm can return non-trivial solutions even applied purely random data — meaning researchers may inadvertently identify patterns artifacts chance rather genuine causal structures. braQCA addresses problem directly two complementary tools: baQCA() — tests whether completed QCA solution robust randomness estimating probability researcher’s data parameters yield non-trivial result chance alone. brQCA() — provides data-driven recommendations consistency score configurational n thresholds needed attain desired levels statistical confidence given QCA application. Together, tools function hypothesis testing framework QCA, producing output analogous p-value researchers can use assess report robustness findings. methodology detailed : Gibson, C. Ben Burrel Vann Jr. 2025. “Bootstrapped Robustness Assessment Qualitative Comparative Analysis.” Journal Mathematical Sociology 40(3): 147–174. doi:10.1080/0022250X.2025.2496154

what: Step 1 — Prepare data and run a QCA model
title: Bootstrapped Robustness Assessment for Qualitative Comparative Analysis
code: library(QCA) library(braQCA)  data(rallies)  # Select causal conditions P <- rallies$P R <- rallies$R C <- rallies$C U <- rallies$U  qca.data <- data.frame(P, R, C, U) rownames(qca.data) <- rownames(rallies)  # Build truth table truth <- truthTable(qca.data, outcome = "P", sort.by = "incl",                     incl.cut1 = 0.7, show.cases = TRUE) truth  # Minimize the truth table mod1 <- minimize(truth, details = TRUE, show.cases = TRUE) mod1

title: Bootstrapped Robustness Assessment for Qualitative Comparative Analysis
text: function returns estimated probability data chosen parameters yield random result, along confidence interval. low value (e.g., < .05) indicates solution unlikely artifact chance.
code: # Test robustness of the solution (use sim=2000 for production; sim=5 for quick testing) baQCA(mod1, sim = 5)

title: Bootstrapped Robustness Assessment for Qualitative Comparative Analysis
text: returns table showing combinations inclcut ncut achieve significance thresholds .10, .05, .01, .001 — helping researchers select defensible parameters finalizing QCA model.
code: qca.data <- rallies[, 8:13]  # Get parameter recommendations (use higher sim for production) brQCA(qca.data, outcome = "P", ncut = 5, sim = 1)

text: mod name QCA model object – minimization truth table. sim number simulations baQCA function run. Default set sim=2000. logical, whether causal conditions outcome resampled (replacement). Default set =TRUE. include [QCA package] “vector additional output function values included minimization.” Default set include=c(""). row.dom [QCA package] “Logical, impose row dominance constraint solution eliminate dominated inessential prime implicants.” Default set FALSE. omit [QCA package] “vector configuration index values matrix configurations omitted minimization.” Default set omit=c(). dir.exp [QCA package] “vector directional expectations deriving intermediate solutions.” Default set dir.exp=c().

title: Bootstrapped Recommendation — brQCA
text: qca.data QCA data frame. outcome outcome variable QCA data frame causal conditions; "" outcome variable application QCA. type QCA application, "crisp" "fuzzy" sets. Default set type = "crisp". inclcut range consistency scores inclusion. specified, defaults seq(= 0.5, = 1, = 0.01). ncut configurational n levels simulate. Can altered give options range minimum maximum ncut value truth table yields, naming truth table object (e.g. truth) calling minimum maximum number cases, using ncut=min(truth$tt$n):max(truth$tt$n) identified truth table. Default set ncut=2. neg.[QCA package] “Logical, use negation outcome (ignored data truth table object).” Default set neg.=FALSE. sim number simulations run combination parameters. final number simulations length(inclcut)*length(ncut)*sim*2. Default set sim=10. verbose prints system time used run simulation percent complete. Default set verbose=TRUE.
